simple.meaning: בָּרִיחַ (bârîyach) is a place-name in the Hebrew text (H1281). BibleIQ follows its 3 occurrences across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This place appears in Job, Isaiah, beginning at Job 26:13. The surrounding context includes Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to the Hebrew place-name בָּרִיחַ (H1281).
simple.whyItMatters: Places in Scripture often connect geography, covenant history, judgment, worship, and movement through the land. BibleIQ keeps the place tied to its actual verse trail.
simple.summary: בָּרִיחַ (bârîyach) / H1281 is traced through Job 26:13, Isaiah 27:1, Isaiah 43:14 using generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.short: a fugitive , i.e. the serpent (as fleeing ), and the constellation by that name
definitions.full: H1281. bariach I. [ בָּרִיחַ ] adjective fleeing ( = ֗֗֗ בַּרִּיחַ ) בִָּרחַ׃ נָחָשׁ Job 26:13 of eclipse-dragon, בָרִחַ נָחָשׁ לִוְיָתָן Isa 27:1 (probably figurative of Assyrians); as substantive בָּרִיחִים 43:14 as fugitives (for other views compare Comm.); so probably also 15:5 בריחיה , see בְּרִיחַ .
